newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv mayor meets Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv mayor meets Arafat.

text.p: Tel Aviv Mayor Roni Milo, a member of Israel's ruling Likud party, held talks on Thursday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in self-ruled Jericho but denied he was on an official mission.
"I cannot speak on behalf of the government," said Milo, who is far removed from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's inner circle. "I am not here on a mission."
But Milo said he and Arafat discussed "the need to move the peace process forward on the subject of Hebron and a meeting between Netanyahu and Arafat (which) I hope will take place soon".

The Israeli media have raised the possibility that Netanyahu and Arafat might meet soon to finalise an elusive agreement on implementing a long overdue Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Netanyahu has accused the Palestinians of deliberately delaying a deal out of a desire to bring international pressure on his right-wing government. Arafat has denied the allegation.
After Netanyahu's election in May, Milo broke party ranks to urge the Likud chief to drop his opposition to meeting Arafat. Both leaders have since met in Gaza and in Washington.
